Suwalki Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Suwałki, Poland

Not demolished. Suwałki's Jewish population reached 12,540 (60.9 percent of the city) in 1890, most later deported at the end of 1939 to Biała Podlaska and Kock, both documented elsewhere in this collection, and killed in the years that followed. This cemetery, established around 1820, began decaying during WWII, when the Germans used tombstones to build a swimming pool and pave streets; in the 1950s, the site was used as a horse market and for cattle grazing, though burials continued as recently as 2010 and 2012. In the 1980s, at the initiative of Rabbi Dawid Lifszyc, the cemetery was fenced and cleaned, with lapidaria arranged from recovered tombstones and a monument funded to commemorate Suwałki's rabbis.
